hints: Identify all forces acting on the ring: the upward pulling tension of $2.5\text{ N}$ at $15^\circ$ to the horizontal, the downward weight $W = mg = 0.03g\text{ N}$, the normal reaction $R$ perpendicular to the vertical rod, and the friction force $F$.
Because the ring is on the point of sliding upwards, the limiting friction force $F$ acts vertically downwards along the rod and satisfies $F = \mu R$.
Resolve horizontally to find the normal reaction $R$ in terms of the tension: $R = 2.5\cos 15^\circ$.
Resolve vertically for equilibrium to set up $2.5\sin 15^\circ = 0.03g + F$, substitute $F = \mu R$, and solve for $\mu$ using $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$.
walkthrough: Identify the forces acting on the ring $P$. The string pulls with tension $T = 2.5\text{ N}$ at $15^\circ$ above the horizontal. The rod exerts a horizontal normal contact force $R$ and a vertical friction force $F$. The earth exerts a downward gravitational force of weight $W = mg$.

State the condition for horizontal equilibrium perpendicular to the vertical rod:
$$\sum F_x = 0$$
$$R - T\cos 15^\circ = 0$$
$$R = 2.5\cos 15^\circ \approx 2.4148\text{ N}$$

State the limiting friction formula. Since the ring is in limiting equilibrium on the point of slipping upwards, friction acts downwards to oppose impending motion:
$$F = \mu R = \mu(2.5\cos 15^\circ)$$

State the condition for vertical equilibrium along the rod:
$$\sum F_y = 0$$
$$T\sin 15^\circ - mg - F = 0$$
$$2.5\sin 15^\circ = 0.03(10) + F$$
$$2.5\sin 15^\circ = 0.3 + F$$

Substitute the expression for friction $F = \mu(2.5\cos 15^\circ)$ into the vertical equilibrium equation:
$$2.5\sin 15^\circ = 0.3 + \mu(2.5\cos 15^\circ)$$
Subtract $0.3$ from both sides:
$$\mu(2.5\cos 15^\circ) = 2.5\sin 15^\circ - 0.3$$
Divide by $2.5\cos 15^\circ$:
$$\mu = \frac{2.5\sin 15^\circ - 0.3}{2.5\cos 15^\circ} = \frac{0.647048 - 0.3}{2.414815} = \frac{0.347048}{2.414815} \approx 0.144$$
